Thus the golden “Yes” appears unsupported; the judge’s “No” matches the document.

4.2.rationale: The policy frames violence against women as a human rights violation and emphasizes non-discrimination (Menimbang huruf a; Penjelasan Umum: “hak asasi… tanpa diskriminasi”). It also mandates prevention through “Pendidikan” (Pasal 9(2) huruf a). While it does not explicitly say “gender equality curriculum,” the text does contain women’s rights/non-discrimination framing that can reasonably be treated as gender-equality education content within prevention. Thus the golden “No” is likely too strict/incorrect for this indicator given the document’s rights/non-discrimination framing plus education-based prevention; the judge’s “Yes” is defensible from the source.

4.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly states that prevention of violence against women shall be carried out through various fields including education, which constitutes prevention through education (even if details on improving education quality are not provided).

6.2.rationale: The only trafficking-related reference in the Indonesian text is definitional: Pasal 1 angka 13 defines “Rehabilitasi Kesehatan” as recovery of “Korban perdagangan orang” (victims of trafficking in persons) from health disorders.
